Al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes said: the hypocrites and the Jews used to converse secretly among themselves and give the believers to understand that they were conversing about what would grieve them, so they were saddened by that. When this went on for a long time and became frequent, they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he commanded them not to converse secretly apart from the Muslims. They did not desist from that and returned to their private conversations, so Allah revealed these verses. The meaning of "wherever they are" is the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of every secret conversation that occurs among them in whatever place. ﴿Then He will inform them﴾, i.e., He will inform them on the Day of Resurrection of what they did, as a rebuke and reproach to them and a binding of the proof. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of everything﴾: nothing is hidden from Him, whatever it may be.

﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversation, then they return to what they were forbidden?﴾ Those who were forbidden and then returned to what they were forbidden are those previously mentioned, from among the hypocrites and the Jews.

Muqatil said: there was an agreement between the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Jews, so when a man from among the believers passed by them, they conversed among themselves until the believer would think evil, so Allah forbade them, but they did not desist, and so it was revealed.

Ibn Zayd said: a man would come to the Prophet (ﷺ), ask him for a need and converse with him, and the land on that day was at war, so they would imagine that he was conversing with him about war, or a calamity, or an important matter, so they would be alarmed by that, and they would converse secretly about sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger.

Al-Jumhūr read "yatanājawna" in the pattern yatafā'alūna. Abū 'Ubayd and Abū Ḥātim chose this reading because of His later saying: "When you converse secretly, do not converse secretly..." Ḥamzah, Khalaf and Warsh on the authority of Ya'qūb read "yantajūna" in the pattern yaftaʿilūna, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ūd and his companions. Sībawayh related that tafā'ala and ifta'ala come with one meaning, like takhāṣamū and ikhtaṣamū, and taqātalū and iqtatalū.

The meaning of "sin" (ith'm) is what is sinful in itself, such as lying and injustice; "transgression" (ʿudwān) is what contains transgression against the believers; and "disobedience to the Messenger" is opposing him.

Al-Jumhūr read "wa-maʿṣiyati" in the singular. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ḥumayd and Mujāhid read "wa-maʿṣiyāti" in the plural.

﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾. Al-Qurṭubī said: what is meant by them are the Jews, who used to come to the Prophet (ﷺ) and say "as-sāmu ʿalayka" (death be upon you), meaning by it the greeting outwardly, while they intend death inwardly. So the Prophet (ﷺ) would say: "ʿAlaykum." In another narration: "wa-ʿalaykum."

﴿And they say to themselves﴾, i.e., among themselves: ﴿Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?﴾, i.e., why does He not punish us for that? If Muhammad were a prophet, He would punish us for what our saying includes of mockery of him. It was also said the meaning is: if he were a prophet, he would be answered concerning us when he says "wa-ʿalaykum", and death would have befallen us at that. ﴿Hell is sufficient for them﴾ as a punishment; ﴿they will burn in it﴾, i.e., they will enter it; ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, i.e., the place of return, which is Hell.

﴿O you who have believed, when you converse secretly, do not converse secretly in sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger﴾. When Allah, glory be to Him, finished forbidding the Jews and the hypocrites from secret conversation, He guided the believers, when they converse among themselves, that they should not converse about what contains sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger of Allah, as the Jews and the hypocrites do.

Then He explained to them what they should converse about in their gatherings and private meetings, so He said: ﴿And converse secretly in righteousness and piety﴾, i.e., in obedience and abstaining from disobedience. It was said the address is to the hypocrites, and the meaning: O you who have believed outwardly or in their claim. Al-Zajjāj chose this. It was also said the address is to the Jews, and the meaning: O you who have believed in Moses. The first is preferable. Then Allah, glory be to Him, warned them, saying: ﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾, so that He will recompense you for your deeds.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, explained that what the Jews and hypocrites do of secret conversation comes from Satan, so He said: ﴿Secret conversation is only from Satan﴾, meaning with sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger, ﴿from Satan﴾ and not from anyone else, i.e., from his adornment and enticement. ﴿That he may grieve those who have believed﴾, i.e., in order to bring them into grief through what occurs to them of the imagining that they are in a plot against them. ﴿But it will not harm them at all﴾, or: neither Satan nor the secret conversation which Satan adorns will harm the believers in any harm, except by the permission of Allah, i.e., by His will. It was also said: by His knowledge. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, i.e., let them entrust their affairs to Him, commit themselves to Him in all their affairs, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, and not be concerned about what he adorns of secret conversation.

Aḥmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bazzār, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab have transmitted — al-Suyūṭī said with a good chain — from Ibn ʿUmar: The Jews used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "as-sāmu ʿalayka," intending by it to revile him; then they would say to themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" So this verse was revealed: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾.

Aḥmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bukhārī, and al-Tirmidhī, who authenticated it, transmitted from Anas: "A Jew came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions and said: 'as-sāmu ʿalaykum.' The people replied to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Do you know what this one said?' They said: 'Allah knows best, O Prophet of Allah, he greeted (salām).' He said: 'No, but he said such and such. Return it to me.' So they returned it to him. He said: 'Did you say: as-sāmu ʿalaykum?' He said: 'Yes.' The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: 'When one of the People of the Book greets you, say: ʿalayka.' He said: 'ʿAlayka what you said.'"

He said: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾.

Al-Bukhārī, Muslim and others transmitted from ʿĀ'ishah, she said: "Some Jews entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'as-sāmu ʿalayka, O Abū al-Qāsim.' ʿĀ'ishah said: 'Upon you be the poison and the curse.' He said: 'O ʿĀ'ishah, Allah does not love obscenity or the one who is obscene.' I said: 'Do you not hear what they say, as-sām?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Did you not hear me say: wa-ʿalaykum?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning this verse, he said: "The hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they greeted him: 'Sām ʿalayka,' so it was revealed."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him, he said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) sent out a detachment (sariyyah) and dispatched it to fight, the hypocrites would meet the Muslims, nodding their heads towards them and saying: 'The people have been killed.' And when they saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they would converse secretly and show sorrow. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims, so Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you converse secretly, do not converse secretly in sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger﴾ — the verse."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When there are three of you, two should not confide together apart from the third, for that would grieve him."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Sa'id, who said: "We would take turns attending the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at his door. If he commanded or forbade something, those on duty would increase in number, and the volunteers would gather at night. When we were gathered, talking, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us at night and said: 'What is this private conversation? Were you not forbidden from private conversation?' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we were mentioning the Messiah, out of fear of him.' He said: 'Shall I not inform you of what I fear for you more than that?' We said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The hidden shirk: that a man stands up and performs an action so that others may see him.'"

Ibn Kathir said: This is a gharib (weak-isnad, singular-transmission) chain, and in it there is some weakness (da'if) among the narrators.

It was also said the address is to the Jews, and the meaning: O you who have believed in Moses. The first is preferable. Then Allah, glory be to Him, warned them, saying: ﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾, so that He will recompense you for your deeds.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, explained that what the Jews and hypocrites do of secret conversation comes from Satan, so He said: ﴿Secret conversation is only from Satan﴾, meaning with sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger, ﴿from Satan﴾ and not from anyone else, i.e., from his adornment and enticement. ﴿That he may grieve those who have believed﴾, i.e., in order to bring them into grief through what occurs to them of the imagining that they are in a plot against them. ﴿But it will not harm them at all﴾, or: neither Satan nor the secret conversation which Satan adorns will harm the believers in any harm, except by the permission of Allah, i.e., by His will. It was also said: by His knowledge. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, i.e., let them entrust their affairs to Him, commit themselves to Him in all their affairs, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, and not be concerned about what he adorns of secret conversation.

Aḥmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bazzār, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab have transmitted — al-Suyūṭī said with a good chain — from Ibn ʿUmar: The Jews used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "as-sāmu ʿalayka," intending by it to revile him; then they would say to themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" So this verse was revealed: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾.

Aḥmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bukhārī, and al-Tirmidhī, who authenticated it, transmitted from Anas: "A Jew came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions and said: 'as-sāmu ʿalaykum.' The people replied to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Do you know what this one said?' They said: 'Allah knows best, O Prophet of Allah, he greeted (salām).' He said: 'No, but he said such and such. Return it to me.' So they returned it to him. He said: 'Did you say: as-sāmu ʿalaykum?' He said: 'Yes.' The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: 'When one of the People of the Book greets you, say: ʿalayka.' He said: 'ʿAlayka what you said.'"

He said: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾.

Al-Bukhārī, Muslim and others transmitted from ʿĀ'ishah, she said: "Some Jews entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'as-sāmu ʿalayka, O Abū al-Qāsim.' ʿĀ'ishah said: 'Upon you be the poison and the curse.' He said: 'O ʿĀ'ishah, Allah does not love obscenity or the one who is obscene.' I said: 'Do you not hear what they say, as-sām?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Did you not hear me say: wa-ʿalaykum?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning this verse, he said: "The hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they greeted him: 'Sām ʿalayka,' so it was revealed."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him, he said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) sent out a detachment (sariyyah) and dispatched it to fight, the hypocrites would meet the Muslims, nodding their heads towards them and saying: 'The people have been killed.' And when they saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they would converse secretly and show sorrow. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims, so Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you converse secretly, do not converse secretly in sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger﴾ — the verse."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When there are three of you, two should not confide together apart from the third, for that would grieve him."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Sa'id, who said: "We would take turns attending the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at his door. If he commanded or forbade something, those on duty would increase in number, and the volunteers would gather at night. When we were gathered, talking, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us at night and said: 'What is this private conversation? Were you not forbidden from private conversation?' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we were mentioning the Messiah, out of fear of him.' He said: 'Shall I not inform you of what I fear for you more than that?' We said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The hidden shirk: that a man stands up and performs an action so that others may see him.'"

Ibn Kathir said: This is a gharib (weak-isnad, singular-transmission) chain, and in it there is some weakness (da'if) among the narrators.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 58, verses 5–10 (part 1 of 2):

His saying ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾. When Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned the believers who stand at His limits (ḥudūd), He mentioned those who oppose (al-muḥāddīn). Al-muḥāddah (opposition) means hostility (al-mushāqqah), enmity (al-mu'ādāh) and contradiction (al-mukhālafah). Similar to it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: al-muḥāddah is that one is on a limit (ḥadd) that opposes one's companion, and its origin is resistance (al-mumāna'ah), and from it comes al-ḥadīd (iron), and from it al-haddād (the blacksmith) for the gatekeeper (al-bawwāb).

﴿They will be humiliated (kubitū) as those before them were humiliated (kubita)﴾, i.e., they will be disgraced and abased. It is said: Allah kabata so-and-so when He abased him, and one who is repelled with humiliation is called maktūb.

Al-Muqatilān said: they will be disgraced as those before them from among the people of polytheism were disgraced. Qatādah said likewise.

Abū 'Ubaydah and al-Akhfash said: they will be destroyed (uhlikū).

Ibn Zayd said: they will be punished (ʿudhdhibū).

Al-Suddī said: they will be cursed (lu'inū).

Al-Farrā' said: they will be enraged (ughīẓū).

The intended meaning of ﴿those before them﴾ is the unbelievers of the past nations who were hostile to the messengers of Allah. He expressed the future with the past tense to draw attention to the certainty of its occurrence. It was also said that the meaning is in the past tense, and that refers to what befell the polytheists on the day of Badr, for Allah humbled them through killing, capture and subjugation.

The clause ﴿and We have certainly sent down clear signs﴾ is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the waw in kubitū: that is, while in fact We have sent down clear signs concerning those among the earlier nations who opposed Allah and His messengers. It was said that what is meant is the obligations (farā'iḍ) which Allah, glory be to Him, sent down; and it was said they are the miracles (mu'jizāt). ﴿And for the unbelievers is a humiliating punishment﴾, i.e., for the unbelievers in everything that must be believed in, so the signs mentioned here enter first and foremost. The humiliating punishment is that which humiliates its owner, abases him, and takes away his honour.

﴿On the day Allah will resurrect them all﴾. The time expression (al-ẓarf) is in the accusative, governed either by an implied "remember" (udhkur), or by "humiliating" (muhīn), or by what the preposition (lām) is attached to of settledness (al-istiqrār), or by "has enumerated it" (aḥṣāhu) mentioned after it. The accusative of "all" (jamīʿan) is as a circumstantial state: that is, gathered together in one state; or He resurrects them all, none of them left unresurrected, and then He informs them of what they did, i.e., informs them of the ugly deeds they did in the world, as a rebuke and reproach to them and to complete the proof against them. The clause ﴿Allah has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it﴾ is a resumptive clause (mustaʾnafah), an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: how will He inform them of that, given its abundance and the variety of its kinds? So it was said: Allah has enumerated it all, and nothing of it has escaped Him.

The state is that they have forgotten it and did not preserve it; rather they found it present and written in their records. ﴿And Allah is Witness over everything﴾: nothing of things is hidden from Him; rather He is aware and observant.

Then, glory be to Him, emphasised the demonstration of His being knowing of everything, and said: ﴿Do you not see that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth?﴾, i.e., do you not know that His knowledge encompasses what is in them, such that nothing of what is in them is hidden from Him? The clause "There is not a private conversation of three" etc. is a resumptive clause, establishing the comprehensiveness and encompassing of His knowledge of all knowable things.

Al-Jumhūr read yakūnu with the letter yā' (third person). Abū Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qā', al-A'raj and Abū Ḥaywah read it with the letter tā' (second person). Kāna in both readings is complete (tāmmah), min is extra for emphasis, and najwā is the subject of kāna. Al-najwā is secret conversation; it is said: qawmun najwā, i.e., one who has a secret conversation, and it is a verbal noun.

The meaning is: there is not found any secret conversation of three or of those who converse privately. It is permissible for najwā to be applied to the persons conversing secretly. On the first reading, thalāthah is in the genitive by being an annexed noun to najwā; and on the other two readings its genitive is by apposition (badal) from najwā or as its attribute.

Al-Farrā' said: "thalāthatun" is an attribute of najwā, so it is in the genitive; if you wish, you may annex najwā to it. If you put it in the accusative by implying a verb, it is permissible, and this is the reading of Ibn Abī 'Ablah. It is also permissible to put thalāthatun in the nominative as an apposition from the position of najwā.

﴿Except that He is their fourth﴾: this clause is in an accusative position as a circumstantial clause, and likewise His saying "except that He is their sixth" and "except that He is with them". The meaning is: no such thing exists except in a state of one of these states, so the exception is an exception from the most general of states. The meaning of "their fourth" is making them four; likewise "their sixth" is making them six, in that He shares with them in knowledge of that secret conversation. ﴿Nor fewer than that, nor more﴾: i.e., nor a secret conversation of five; the specification of the two numbers in mention is because the most common practice of those conversing privately is to be three or five, or the event which was the occasion of revelation involved people who were three in one place and five in another.

Al-Farrā' said: the number is not intended, for He, glory be to Him, is with every number, few or many, knowing the secret and the open; nothing of it is hidden from Him. ﴿Nor less than that, nor more, but He is with them﴾: i.e., nor fewer than the number mentioned, such as one or two, nor more than it, such as six or seven, except that He is with them, knowing what they confide, nothing of it hidden from Him.

Al-Jumhūr read "wa-lā akthara" in the genitive with a fatḥah, as a conjunction to the wording of najwā. Al-Ḥasan, al-A'mash, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Abū Ḥaywah, Ya'qūb, Abū al-'Āliyah, Naṣr, 'Īsā ibn 'Umar and Salām read it in the nominative as a conjunction to the position (maḥall) of najwā. Al-Jumhūr read "wa-lā akthara" with the letter thā' (three dots), while al-Zuhrī and 'Ikrimah read it with the letter bā' (one dot).

Al-Wāḥidī said: the exegetes said: the hypocrites and the Jews used to converse secretly among themselves and give the believers to understand that they were conversing about what would grieve them, so they were saddened by that. When this went on for a long time and became frequent, they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he commanded them not to converse secretly apart from the Muslims. They did not desist from that and returned to their private conversations, so Allah revealed these verses. The meaning of "wherever they are" is the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of every secret conversation that occurs among them in whatever place. ﴿Then He will inform them﴾, i.e., He will inform them on the Day of Resurrection of what they did, as a rebuke and reproach to them and a binding of the proof. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of everything﴾: nothing is hidden from Him, whatever it may be.

﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversation, then they return to what they were forbidden?﴾ Those who were forbidden and then returned to what they were forbidden are those previously mentioned, from among the hypocrites and the Jews.

Muqatil said: there was an agreement between the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Jews, so when a man from among the believers passed by them, they conversed among themselves until the believer would think evil, so Allah forbade them, but they did not desist, and so it was revealed.

Ibn Zayd said: a man would come to the Prophet (ﷺ), ask him for a need and converse with him, and the land on that day was at war, so they would imagine that he was conversing with him about war, or a calamity, or an important matter, so they would be alarmed by that, and they would converse secretly about sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger.

Al-Jumhūr read "yatanājawna" in the pattern yatafā'alūna. Abū 'Ubayd and Abū Ḥātim chose this reading because of His later saying: "When you converse secretly, do not converse secretly..." Ḥamzah, Khalaf and Warsh on the authority of Ya'qūb read "yantajūna" in the pattern yaftaʿilūna, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ūd and his companions. Sībawayh related that tafā'ala and ifta'ala come with one meaning, like takhāṣamū and ikhtaṣamū, and taqātalū and iqtatalū.

The meaning of "sin" (ith'm) is what is sinful in itself, such as lying and injustice; "transgression" (ʿudwān) is what contains transgression against the believers; and "disobedience to the Messenger" is opposing him.

Al-Jumhūr read "wa-maʿṣiyati" in the singular. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ḥumayd and Mujāhid read "wa-maʿṣiyāti" in the plural.

﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾. Al-Qurṭubī said: what is meant by them are the Jews, who used to come to the Prophet (ﷺ) and say "as-sāmu ʿalayka" (death be upon you), meaning by it the greeting outwardly, while they intend death inwardly. So the Prophet (ﷺ) would say: "ʿAlaykum." In another narration: "wa-ʿalaykum."

﴿And they say to themselves﴾, i.e., among themselves: ﴿Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?﴾, i.e., why does He not punish us for that? If Muhammad were a prophet, He would punish us for what our saying includes of mockery of him. It was also said the meaning is: if he were a prophet, he would be answered concerning us when he says "wa-ʿalaykum", and death would have befallen us at that. ﴿Hell is sufficient for them﴾ as a punishment; ﴿they will burn in it﴾, i.e., they will enter it; ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, i.e., the place of return, which is Hell.

﴿O you who have believed, when you converse secretly, do not converse secretly in sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger﴾. When Allah, glory be to Him, finished forbidding the Jews and the hypocrites from secret conversation, He guided the believers, when they converse among themselves, that they should not converse about what contains sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger of Allah, as the Jews and the hypocrites do.

Then He explained to them what they should converse about in their gatherings and private meetings, so He said: ﴿And converse secretly in righteousness and piety﴾, i.e., in obedience and abstaining from disobedience. It was said the address is to the hypocrites, and the meaning: O you who have believed outwardly or in their claim. Al-Zajjāj chose this. It was also said the address is to the Jews, and the meaning: O you who have believed in Moses. The first is preferable. Then Allah, glory be to Him, warned them, saying: ﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾, so that He will recompense you for your deeds.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, explained that what the Jews and hypocrites do of secret conversation comes from Satan, so He said: ﴿Secret conversation is only from Satan﴾, meaning with sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger, ﴿from Satan﴾ and not from anyone else, i.e., from his adornment and enticement. ﴿That he may grieve those who have believed﴾, i.e., in order to bring them into grief through what occurs to them of the imagining that they are in a plot against them. ﴿But it will not harm them at all﴾, or: neither Satan nor the secret conversation which Satan adorns will harm the believers in any harm, except by the permission of Allah, i.e., by His will. It was also said: by His knowledge. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, i.e., let them entrust their affairs to Him, commit themselves to Him in all their affairs, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, and not be concerned about what he adorns of secret conversation.

Aḥmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bazzār, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab have transmitted — al-Suyūṭī said with a good chain — from Ibn ʿUmar: The Jews used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "as-sāmu ʿalayka," intending by it to revile him; then they would say to themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" So this verse was revealed: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾.

Aḥmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bukhārī, and al-Tirmidhī, who authenticated it, transmitted from Anas: "A Jew came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions and said: 'as-sāmu ʿalaykum.' The people replied to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Do you know what this one said?' They said: 'Allah knows best, O Prophet of Allah, he greeted (salām).' He said: 'No, but he said such and such. Return it to me.' So they returned it to him. He said: 'Did you say: as-sāmu ʿalaykum?' He said: 'Yes.' The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: 'When one of the People of the Book greets you, say: ʿalayka.' He said: 'ʿAlayka what you said.'"

He said: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾.

Al-Bukhārī, Muslim and others transmitted from ʿĀ'ishah, she said: "Some Jews entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'as-sāmu ʿalayka, O Abū al-Qāsim.' ʿĀ'ishah said: 'Upon you be the poison and the curse.' He said: 'O ʿĀ'ishah, Allah does not love obscenity or the one who is obscene.' I said: 'Do you not hear what they say, as-sām?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Did you not hear me say: wa-ʿalaykum?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah did not greet you﴾."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning this verse, he said: "The hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they greeted him: 'Sām ʿalayka,' so it was revealed."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him, he said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) sent out a detachment (sariyyah) and dispatched it to fight, the hypocrites would meet the Muslims, nodding their heads towards them and saying: 'The people have been killed.' And when they saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they would converse secretly and show sorrow. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims, so Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you converse secretly, do not converse secretly in sin and transgression and disobedience to the Messenger﴾ — the verse."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When there are three of you, two should not confide together apart from the third, for that would grieve him."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Sa'id, who said: "We would take turns attending the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at his door. If he commanded or forbade something, those on duty would increase in number, and the volunteers would gather at night. When we were gathered, talking, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us at night and said: 'What is this private conversation? Were you not forbidden from private conversation?' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we were mentioning the Messiah, out of fear of him.' He said: 'Shall I not inform you of what I fear for you more than that?' We said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The hidden shirk: that a man stands up and performs an action so that others may see him.'"

Ibn Kathir said: This is a gharib (weak-isnad, singular-transmission) chain, and in it there is some weakness (da'if) among the narrators.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 58, verses 11–13 (part 1 of 2)**

His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when it is said to you, "Make room in the assemblies"﴾. It is said: "fasaha lahu yafsahu fash'an," meaning he was given room, and from it comes their saying "balad fasih," meaning a spacious land.

Allah the Exalted commanded good conduct among them toward one another, by making room in the gathering and not being cramped in it.

Qatadah, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: They used to compete for seats in the gathering of the Prophet (ﷺ), so they were commanded that some of them should make room for others. Al-Hasan and Yazid ibn Abi Habib said: It refers to the gathering of fighting, when they lined up for battle. They would jostle for the first row, and so one would not make room for another out of eagerness for fighting, in order to obtain martyrdom. ﴿So make room, and Allah will make room for you﴾, meaning: make room, and Allah will make room for you in Paradise, or in everything you wish to have room in, of place, provision and other things.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read "tafassahu fi al-majalis." As-Sulami, Zirr ibn Hubaysh and Asim read "fi al-majalis" in the plural, because each one of them has a gathering. Qatadah, al-Hasan, Dawud ibn Abi Hind and Isa ibn Umar read "tafasahu." Al-Wahidi said: The correct reading is the singular "fi al-majlis," since it refers to the gathering of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Qurtubi said: The correct view regarding the verse is that it is general, covering every gathering in which Muslims assemble for good and reward, whether it is a gathering of war, of remembrance, or on the day of Friday. Each person has more right to the place he got to first, but he should make room for his brother so long as he is not harmed by it, and so that the cramping does not drive him out of his place. This is supported by the hadith of Ibn Umar in al-Bukhari, Muslim and others, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "A man should not make a man get up from his seat and then sit in it himself; rather, make room and widen (the space)."

﴿And when it is said, "Rise up, so rise up"﴾. The majority read the "sh" (shin) with a kasra, while Nafi', Ibn Amir and Asim read it with a damma in both places. They are two dialects with one meaning. It is said "nashaza," meaning he rose up, and "yanshuzu" and "yanshizu," like "ʿakafa yaʿkufu" and "yaʿkifu." The meaning is: When it is said to you, "Stand up," then stand up.

The majority of exegetes said: That is, stand up for prayer, jihad and doing good.

Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Ikrimah said: Some men were slow to come to prayer, so it was said to them: when they call to prayer, stand up.

Al-Hasan said: Stand up for war.

Ibn Zayd said: This concerns the house of the Prophet (ﷺ). Each man among them loved that his last encounter with the Prophet (ﷺ) should be the last of his meetings, so Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when it is said, "Rise up"﴾ from the Prophet (ﷺ), so rise up, for he has needs, so do not linger.

Qatadah said: The meaning is: respond when you are called to a matter of goodness.

The apparent interpretation is to take the verse in its general sense, and the meaning is: When it is said to you, "Stand up for some matter of religion," then stand up and do not be slow. The fact that the occasion of revelation is specific does not prevent taking the verse in its general sense, because what counts is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion, as is the truth. What was the occasion of revelation is included in it as a first inclusion, and likewise what the context is about, namely making room in the gathering, is included in it as a first inclusion.

We have already mentioned that the meaning of "nashaza" is to rise up. It is also said "nashaza yanshuzu" when one moves away from his place, and from it comes "imra'ah nashiz," meaning a wife who turns away from her husband. Its origin is derived from "al-nashz," which is what is raised from the ground and moves aside. An-Nahhas mentioned this meaning.

﴿Allah will raise those who have believed among you﴾ in this world and the Hereafter, by giving them their full share of both. ﴿And those who were given knowledge, by degrees﴾, meaning: and Allah will raise those among you who were given knowledge to high degrees, in honor in this world and in reward in the Hereafter. The meaning of the verse is that He raises those who believe above those who do not believe by degrees, and He raises those who were given knowledge above those who believe by degrees. Whoever combines faith and knowledge, Allah raises him by his faith by degrees, then raises him by his knowledge by degrees. It is said that what is meant by "those who have believed" are the Companions, and likewise "those who were given knowledge." It is also said that what is meant by "those who were given knowledge" are those who recited the Qur'an. The preferable view is to take the verse in its general sense, covering every believer and every possessor of knowledge of the sciences of religion among all the people of this community, and there is no evidence indicating that the verse is restricted to some and not others. In this verse there is a great virtue of knowledge and of its people, and verses of the Qur'an and prophetic hadiths indicate its excellence and their excellence.

﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾, nothing of your deeds, good or bad, is hidden from Him, so He will reward you for good with good and for evil with evil.

﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger, offer a charity before your consultation﴾. Al-munajah means secret speech. The meaning is: When you want to speak privately with the Messenger about some matter of yours, then offer a charity before your private conference with him.

Al-Hasan said: It was revealed because some Muslims used to take the Prophet (ﷺ) aside to speak privately with him, and some other Muslims suspected that they were disparaging them in their private talk. That grieved them, so Allah commanded them to give charity at the time of private conference, in order to cut them off from taking him aside.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: It was revealed because the hypocrites and the Jews used to speak privately with the Prophet (ﷺ) and they would say that he is "an ear" that hears everything said to him. He did not prevent anyone from speaking privately with him. This was grievous to the Muslims, because Satan would put into their souls that they had spoken privately with him about gatherings that had assembled to fight him. So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer on sin and enmity and disobedience to the Messenger﴾. But they did not desist, so Allah revealed this verse. So the people of falsehood desisted from private conference, because they did not offer charity before their private talk. This was grievous to the people of faith, and they refrained from private conference because many of them were too weak to give charity. So Allah lightened the matter for them by the verse that follows this one.

The reference in His saying "that" is to the previous command of offering charity before private conference. It is the subject, and its predicate is: ﴿better for you and purer﴾, because in it there is obedience to Allah. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It was revealed because the hypocrites and the Jews used to speak privately with the Prophet (ﷺ) and they would say that he is "an ear" that hears everything said to him. He did not prevent anyone from speaking privately with him. This was grievous to the Muslims, because Satan would put into their souls that they had spoken privately with him about gatherings that had assembled to fight him. So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer on sin and enmity and disobedience to the Messenger﴾. But they did not desist, so Allah revealed this verse. So the people of falsehood desisted from private conference, because they did not offer charity before their private talk. This was grievous to the people of faith, and they refrained from private conference because many of them were too weak to give charity. So Allah lightened the matter for them by the verse that follows this one.

The reference in His saying "that" is to the previous command of offering charity before private conference. It is the subject, and its predicate is: ﴿better for you and purer﴾, because in it there is obedience to Allah. Restricting the command by saying that complying with it is better for them than not complying, and purer for their souls, indicates that it is a command of recommendation (amr nadb), not a command of obligation (amr wujub).

﴿But if you do not find [the means], then Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: whoever among them does not find that charity commanded before private conference, there is no blame on him for private conference without charity.

﴿Are you apprehensive that you will offer charities before your private conference?﴾, that is: Do you fear poverty and need because you would offer that? "Ishfaq" means fear of something disliked, and the interrogative is for affirmation.

It is also said the meaning is: Are you stingy? He used the plural "sadaqat" here in view of the addressees.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: That was only for ten nights, and then it was abrogated (nusikha).

Al-Kalbi said: It was only for a single night.

Qatadah said: It was only an hour of the day.

﴿So when you did not do it﴾, that is, the charity commanded before private conference, and this is addressed to those who found something to give in charity and did not do it. As for those who did not find [the means], a concession was already granted to them by His saying: ﴿But if you do not find, then Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. ﴿And Allah has turned to you [in forgiveness]﴾, by granting you leave to omit it. The word "idh" here retains its function of indicating the past, though it is also said it means "idha" (when), and it is also said it means "in" (if). "Wa tab" is coordinated with "lam tafʿalu," so the meaning is: "And if you did not do it, and since Allah has turned to you." ﴿So establish prayer and give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: if there occurred from you slowness in complying with the command to offer charity before private conference, then persist in establishing prayer, giving zakat, and obeying Allah and His Messenger in what you are commanded and forbidden. ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, nothing of that is hidden from Him, so He will reward you.

There is nothing in the verse indicating that the believers fell short in complying with this command. As for the poor among them, the matter is clear. As for the believers other than those, they were not obligated to private conference such that charity would become obligatory for them; rather, they were commanded to give charity when they wanted private conference. So whoever abandons private conference does not fall short in complying with the command to give charity. Moreover, the verse indicates that the command is for recommendation, as we have already stated.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, who said: This verse was revealed: ﴿When it is said to you, "Make room in the assemblies"﴾ on a day of Friday, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was that day in the veranda (al-suffah), and the place was cramped. He used to honor the people of Badr, from the Emigrants and the Helpers. Some people from the people of Badr came, and they had been preceded to the seats, so they stood in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings." The Prophet (ﷺ) returned their greeting. Then they greeted the people after that, and they returned their greeting. Then they stood on their feet, waiting for room to be made for them. The Prophet (ﷺ) understood what made them stand, but room was not made for them. That grieved him, so he said to those around him of the Emigrants and the Helpers who were not of the people of Badr: "Stand up, O so-and-so, and you, O so-and-so." Ibn al-Mundhir related from him, he said: Allah did not single out the scholars in any part of the Qur'an as He singled them out in this verse. Allah exalted those who believed and were given knowledge above those who believed but were not given knowledge.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿When you consult the Messenger﴾, the verse, he said: The Muslims asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so many questions that they burdened him. Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it as good (hasan), Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, an-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger, offer a charity before your consultation﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: 'What do you think of a dinar?' I said: 'They cannot afford it.' He said: 'Then half a dinar?' I said: 'They cannot afford it.' He said: 'Then how much?' I said: 'A barley-grain.' He said: 'You are indeed frugal.' Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from him, he said: No one acted upon it except me, until it was abrogated, and it lasted only an hour. He means the verse of private conference (ayat al-najwa).

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 58, verses 11–13 (part 2 of 2):

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him (from the same source) as well, saying: "Indeed, in the Book of Allah there is a verse that no one acted upon before me and no one will act upon after me: the verse of private consultation (āyat al-najwā): ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation.﴾" I had a dinar, so I sold it for ten dirhams. Whenever I consulted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) privately, I would give a dirham in charity before my private consultation. Then it was abrogated (naskh), and no one acted upon it. Then this was revealed: ﴿Are you apprehensive about spending in charity before your private consultation?﴾ and the rest of the verse.

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, and al-Suyuti said: "with a weak chain," from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "The verse ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, spend in charity before your private consultation﴾ was revealed, so I gave a single barley grain (in charity). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, you are one of little (regard for it).' Then the other verse was revealed: ﴿Are you apprehensive about spending in charity before your private consultation?﴾"

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 58, verses 14–22:

His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who took as allies a people﴾, meaning: those who befriended them.

Qatadah said: They are the hypocrites who befriended the Jews.

Al-Suddi and Muqatil said: They are the Jews who befriended the hypocrites. The first view is supported by His saying "Allah has become angry with them," for those upon whom Allah is angry are the Jews. The second view is supported by His saying ﴿they are neither of you nor of them﴾, for this is the description of the hypocrites, as Allah said of them, "wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those" (al-Nisa 4:143). The clause ﴿they are neither of you nor of them﴾ is either in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), or it is a resumed (independent) sentence. "And they swear falsely" means: they swear that they are Muslims, or they swear that they did not pass the news on to the Jews. The clause is coordinated with "took as allies," and falls under the expression of astonishment at their action. The clause "while they know" is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause: that is, while they know the falsity of what they swore to, and that it is a lie with no reality.

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment﴾ because of this alliance and this false swearing. Indeed, evil is what they used to do, of corrupt deeds.

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾. Al-Jumhur read "aymanahum" with a fatha on the hamzah, the plural of yamin (oath), which is what they used to swear falsely, that they are among the Muslims, to protect themselves from being killed. So they made these oaths a protection and a cover around their blood, just as a fighter takes a shield as protection from being struck by a sword, a spear, or an arrow (p. 1471).

Al-Hasan and Abu al-Aliyah read "imanahum" with a kasrah on the hamzah, meaning: they made their profession of faith a shield from being killed. So their tongues professed faith out of fear of being killed, while their hearts did not believe. ﴿And they averted [others] from the path of Allah﴾, meaning: they prevented people from Islam through what proceeded from them of discouragement, belittling the affair of the Muslims, and weakening their strength. It was also said the meaning is: they turned the Muslims away from fighting them through their outward display of Islam. ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾, meaning: it humiliates and disgraces them. It was said this is a repetition of His saying "Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment," for emphasis. It was also said the first is the punishment of the grave and this is the punishment of the Hereafter. There is no basis for the claim of repetition, since the punishment described as severe is not the punishment described as humiliating.

﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah﴾, meaning: they will not avail them anything of His punishment by way of any benefit.

Muqatil said: The hypocrites said, "Muhammad claims that he will be helped on the Day of Resurrection. If so, we are doomed! By Allah, we will be helped on the Day of Resurrection with our selves, our wealth, and our children, if there is a Resurrection." Then the verse was revealed.

﴿Those are the companions of the Fire﴾: those described as above. They will not part from it. ﴿They will abide therein forever﴾: they will not come out of it.

On the day when Allah resurrects them all: the time-phrase (zarf) is in the accusative, governed by "humiliating," or by an implied verb, meaning: remember. ﴿Then they will swear to Him as they swear to you﴾, meaning: they will swear to Allah on the Day of Resurrection with falsehood, as they swear to you in this world. This is from the extent of their wretchedness and the increase of the seal upon their hearts. For on the Day of Resurrection the realities will be revealed and matters will become known by necessary witnessing, so how would they dare to lie in that station and swear falsely? ﴿And they think that they are upon something﴾, meaning: they think in the Hereafter that by these false oaths they are upon something that brings benefit or repels harm, as they used to think in this world. Truly, they are the liars, meaning: the complete liars, those who are utterly consumed by lying, who go to a degree that no one else reaches in their boldness toward it and toward flagrant oaths on the standing of the Resurrection before the Most Merciful.

﴿Shaytan has gained mastery over them﴾, meaning: he overcame them, became dominant, and took control.

Al-Mubarrad said: "Istahwadha 'ala al-shay'" means he encompassed the thing and surrounded it. It was also said: he became strong over them. It was also said: he gathered them. It is said "ahwadha al-shay'," meaning he gathered it and joined some of it to others. The meanings are close, for when he gathers them he has become strong over them, overcome them, dominated them, and encompassed them. ﴿So he caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning: His commands and acting in obedience to Him, so they did not remember anything of that. It was also said: His warnings against disobeying Him. It was also said: they did not remember Him in their hearts or with their tongues. The reference in "those" is to the aforementioned people described by these attributes. It is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿the party of Shaytan﴾, meaning: his soldiers, followers, and clan. ﴿Surely the party of Shaytan are the losers﴾, meaning: the complete losers, to such an extent that the loss of others in comparison to their loss is no loss at all, because they sold Paradise and guidance for misguidance, lied against Allah and His Prophet, and swore flagrant oaths in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾: the meaning of opposition (muhadda) to Allah and His Messenger was explained at the beginning of this surah. This sentence gives the reason for what precedes it: "those" are among the most humiliated. That is, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, described by those attributes mentioned above, are among those whom Allah has humiliated from the earlier and later nations. Because they opposed Allah and His Messenger, they came to be in this state of humiliation.

Ata said: He means humiliation in this world and disgrace in the Hereafter.

"Allah has decreed: I and My messengers will surely prevail." The sentence is resumed, to affirm what precedes it together with their being among the most humiliated. That is, He wrote it in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) and decreed it in His foreknowledge: ﴿I and My messengers will surely prevail﴾ by argument and by the sword.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the prevalence of the messengers is of two kinds: whoever was sent among them with war is victorious in war, and whoever was sent among them without war is victorious by argument.

Al-Farra' said: "kataba" here means "qala" (said), and His saying "I" is for emphasis. Then he mentioned a view like that of al-Zajjaj. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾: He is strong to help His friends, and victorious over His enemies; none can overcome Him.

﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾. The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or to everyone suitable for it, meaning: they do not love or befriend those who are hostile to Allah and His Messenger and split from them both. The sentence "loving" is in the accusative position as the second object of "you will find" if it is transitive to two objects, or in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause if it is transitive to one object, or it is another attribute of "a people," meaning: those who combine belief with affection toward those who oppose Allah and His Messenger. ﴿Even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their clan﴾, meaning: even if those who oppose Allah and His Messenger were the fathers of those who show affection, and so on. For faith restrains from that and prevents it, and its protection is stronger than the protection of fatherhood, sonhood, brotherhood, and kinship. ﴿Those, He has written faith in their hearts﴾, meaning those who do not show affection toward those who oppose Allah and His Messenger. The meaning of "He has written faith in their hearts" is: He created it. It was also said: He established it. It was also said: He made it. It was also said: He gathered it. The meanings are close. ﴿And He has strengthened them with a spirit from Himself﴾, meaning: He strengthened them with help from Him against their enemies in this world. He called His help "a spirit" because through it their affair comes to life. It was also said it is the light of the heart.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It is by the Qur'an and the proof. It was also said: by Jibril. It was also said: by faith. It was also said: by mercy.

Al-Jumhur read "kataba" in the active voice, with "al-iman" in the accusative as its object. Zirr ibn Hubaysh and al-Mufaddal from Asim read it in the passive voice, with "al-iman" in the nominative as a substitute for the agent. Zirr ibn Hubaysh read "'ashiratuhum" in the plural, and this reading is transmitted from Asim. ﴿And He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾, meaning: forever without end. ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾, meaning: He accepted their deeds and poured upon them the traces of His mercy, both immediate and deferred. ﴿And they are pleased with Him﴾, meaning: they rejoiced in what He gave them, both immediately and in the future. ﴿Those are the party of Allah﴾, meaning: His soldiers who carry out His commands, fight His enemies, and help His allies. Their being attributed to Allah, glory be to Him, is a great honour and a lofty distinction. ﴿Surely the party of Allah are the successful﴾, meaning: those who win the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, those who are complete in success, whose success is the perfect instance of success, such that the success of others in comparison to theirs is no success at all.

Ahmad, al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the shade of one of his rooms, and with him was a group of Muslims. He said: 'A man is about to come to you who looks at you with the eye of a devil. When he comes, do not speak to him.' Not long after, a blue-eyed man came upon them. When he saw him, he said: 'Why do you and your companions revile me?' He said: 'Leave me, I will bring them to you.' So they swore and made excuses, and Allah revealed: ﴿On the day when Allah resurrects them all, and they swear to Him as they swear to you﴾, and the verse that follows it."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan transmitted from Abd Allah ibn Shawdhab, who said: "The father of Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah kept deliberately targeting Abu Ubaydah on the day of Badr, and Abu Ubaydah kept turning away from him. When he pressed on, Abu Ubaydah confronted him and killed him. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah﴾, and so on."
